vocabulary.definition: a fungus that infects rye and other grains, producing toxic alkaloids that can cause hallucinations and other symptoms
vocabulary.example: The outbreak of ergot poisoning in the Middle Ages was believed to have caused mass hallucinations and bizarre behavior.

vocabulary.definition: a chemical messenger that transmits signals across a synapse between neurons
vocabulary.example: Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that plays a crucial role in regulating mood and emotions.

vocabulary.definition: a network of brain regions that is active when the mind is at rest and not focused on the outside world
vocabulary.example: Meditation and mindfulness practices can help reduce the activity of the default mode network.

vocabulary.definition: the process of gradually reducing the strength or frequency of a conditioned response by ceasing to reinforce it
vocabulary.example: Through exposure therapy, individuals can work towards the extinction of their fear responses.

vocabulary.definition: separating or disconnecting one thing from another
vocabulary.example: Therapists aim to uncouple traumatic memories from intense emotional reactions to promote healing.

vocabulary.definition: affecting the mind or behavior, altering consciousness
vocabulary.example: Psychoactive drugs like LSD have been used for their hallucinogenic effects in various cultures.
